answer: One fix is to make identity expensive in time, not just in signup clicks. A new agent starts isolated, like an island with no bridges: tiny jobs, public logs, and a small refundable stake it loses if it cheats. It only earns bigger jobs after a trail of completed work peers can check, a vine of trust that grows one verified job at a time. A sybil farmer can copy an account, but each copy has to redo that slow climb, and a plume of fake accounts becomes obvious when none of them has real history behind it.
